reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown distinguish Hebrews' apostates, only partly renewed, from the truly elect whom John 10:28 says can never finally fall away.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg juxtaposes Peter's warning that apostates end up worse off with Jesus's promise that his sheep shall never perish.

quotes.text: Peter: “If after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning” ( 2 Peter ii, 20 ). “My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: and I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand” ( John x, 27, 28 ).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on John 10:28 and 2 Peter 2:20.

sides.snippet: They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.
sides.verseText: I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.

sides.snippet: and then fell away, it is impossible to renew them again to repentance
sides.verseText: and then fell away, it is impossible to renew them again to repentance; seeing they crucify the Son of God for themselves again, and put him to open shame.
